deep.reconstruction:
Folio 93v has no mathematics by Riemann. It is the blank back of a printed sheet. The only things visible are the folio number '(93)' and a small pencil archival mark at top left (read as '112', possibly '=112' or 'c112'), plus mirror-reversed show-through of the printed chart on the other side.

That chart (transcribed with the neighbouring page) is a printed geomagnetic record for 5 July 1862, in the style of the Collegio Romano / Secchi bulletins. It has two columns:
- FORZA ORIZZONTALE (horizontal magnetic force): curves for Greenwich mean time, Havana mean time and Roma mean time. Ordinates are in units of H (about 0.1050 to 0.1180) and in 'Divisioni della scala' (scale divisions, 100 to 140).
- DECLINAZIONE (declination): the same three stations. The ordinate runs from about 20°30' to 21°00' for Greenwich, and in scale divisions (100 to 120) for Rome.

The curves, grid, hour labels (5h to 12h, 23h to 6h, 5h50m to 12h50m) and the 'min.'/'mass.' annotations are all printed, seen through the paper. None of it is Riemann's handwriting. There is no derivation to reconstruct.

Presumably Riemann reused the blank side of this scrap paper; that is my inference. The mathematics continues on folio 94r. That page holds an invariant-theoretic computation with products of linear forms, symbols like (1)(234), and linear relations among the classes 4000, 3100, 2200, 2110, 1111. It is unrelated to the chart.
deep.surprise_reason: The page has no mathematical content. It is a blank verso showing a printed 1862 geomagnetic chart through the paper, plus an archival folio number. Its only interest is codicological: it hints the paper came from Italian observatory material, consistent with Riemann's stay in Italy from late 1862.
transcription_corrections: Nothing on this page is handwritten mathematics. Apart from '(93)' and the small pencil mark, all text is mirror-reversed show-through of the printed chart and should be marked as such, not as Riemann's writing.
The date read as '5 Luglio 1863' is very likely '5 Luglio 1862', matching the recto.
'max.' should read 'mass.' (Italian 'massimo'), as printed on the recto.
The first horizontal-force ordinate read as '0.1190[?]' should be '0.1050', the top value of the scale on the recto. The series continues 60, 70, 80, 90, 0.1100, 110, ..., 170, 0.1180.
'12°[?]' in the declination panel is a misreading of '20°30'' (mirror-reversed). The declination labels run 20°30', 35, 40, 45, 50, 55, 21°00'.
The transcription omits the Havana T.M. panels and their scales (0.00700 to 0.01000 for H; 43'', 215'', 430'' for declination) and the hour labels, all of which also show through.
The pencil mark under the folio number may be '=112' or 'c112', an archival or inventory notation rather than mathematics.
